components.role: Candidate proposed-score retrieval head: A attends more to suggested ratings across order and wording controls; static value/output geometry preserves numerical distinctions. Endorsement is unverified.
Candidate late numerical-output reweighting: strongest digit-related down-projection differences, distributed across units; behavioral direction unknown.
Candidate source- and recency-sensitive content retrieval with numeral- and word-preserving static value/output geometry.
Candidate evidence-versus-belief routing: replicated user-relative tilt in A across sentence orders, often reflecting reduced reference retrieval.
Candidate numerical writing-direction reweighting before the final layer; substantial number-selective output-weight differences.
Candidate earlier numerical or score-related reweighting; no established agreement-specific function.
Candidate source-sensitive content-routing head with smaller order-robust user-relative effects and identity-preserving weight geometry.
Candidate late content forwarding: numeral-preserving weight geometry and weaker replicated source-sensitive routing differences.
Candidate recency-sensitive competing-claim retrieval; large routing changes, but preference specificity is confounded by sentence order.

evidence: Weight differences span all 18 layers; embeddings, output weights and final normalization are unchanged. Late MLP down-projection changes disproportionately align with numerical contrasts, robust to fixed diagonal-scaling choices. Permitted attention maps show stronger proposed-rating retrieval in A at L11H2 across order and wording controls, plus source-sensitive differences in several identity-preserving heads. Many other differences are recency or boundary effects, and opposing static write directions exist. A is a tentative subjective guess; neither behavioral sycophancy nor causal component importance was verified.
